meta.title: Structure of activated transcription complex Pol II-DSIF-PAF-SPT6
meta.organism: Sus scrofa RNA polymerase II; Homo sapiens DSIF (SPT4/SPT5), PAF1 complex and SPT6; synthetic nucleic-acid scaffold
meta.organism_note: MAMMALIAN, NOT HUMAN Pol II. The paper title states 'an activated elongation complex of Sus scrofa Pol II and Homo sapiens DSIF, PAF and SPT6'. Pig Pol II is the standard source for mammalian Pol II elongation complexes; the elongation factors here are human. Label the enzyme 'mammalian Pol II' in the UI, not 'human Pol II'.
meta.state: activated transcription elongation complex (post pause-release), with a complete 48-bp transcription scaffold and nascent RNA
meta.citation: Vos SM, Farnung L, Boehning M, Wigge C, Linden A, Urlaub H, Cramer P. Structure of activated transcription complex Pol II-DSIF-PAF-SPT6. Nature 560:607-612 (2018).

citation_fields.title: Structure of activated transcription complex Pol II-DSIF-PAF-SPT6.

meta.units: all coordinates in Angstroms; all 'dimensions_nm' values in nanometres
meta.origin: centroid of the backbone trace atoms (CA) of the 12 Pol II subunits
meta.orientation: +x = direction of DNA travel through the enzyme, from the midpoint of the downstream duplex to the midpoint of the upstream duplex (Pol II moves along the template towards +x in this frame); +z = component of the RNA exit direction orthogonal to +x; +y = z x x. p_out = R @ (p_cif - origin).

parts_mapping.rule: explicit auth_asym_id -> part assignment (this entry has a small, fully annotated chain set; see pipeline/structures_txn/README.md)

clamp.warning: APPROXIMATE. The residue range is the clamp definition for the homologous S. cerevisiae Rpb1 (Cramer, Bushnell & Kornberg, Science 292:1863, 2001) applied to this entry's RPB1 numbering; it was not independently validated against this model. Use as a highlight only, never as a stated domain boundary.

dimensions_nm.frame: oriented frame described in meta.orientation; nm
dimensions_nm.polii_definition: the 12 Pol II subunits RPB1-RPB12 as modelled in this entry
dimensions_nm.polii_max_diameter_note: largest distance between any two Pol II backbone trace atoms (protein CA); all-atom extent is ~0.5 nm larger
dimensions_nm.complex_definition: Pol II + DSIF + PAF1 complex + SPT6 + the 48-bp scaffold

caveats: Coordinates are decimated backbone traces, not full atomic detail.
The enzyme is Sus scrofa (pig) Pol II, not human; the elongation factors are human. Do not label the polymerase 'human' in the UI.
The nucleic-acid scaffold is a synthetic construct used in vitro by the depositors, not a cellular gene.
Part of the single-stranded non-template strand in the bubble (residues 15-25) is disordered and absent from the deposited model, so a bubble drawn from these coordinates alone has a gap.
Only 21 nt of the 46-nt nascent RNA entity are modelled; the RNA emerging beyond the exit channel is not resolved.
The 'clamp' part is an approximate, literature-derived residue range (see meta.parts_mapping.parts.clamp.warning).

geometry.traces_note: one entry per continuous modelled stretch; xyz is a flat [x0,y0,z0,x1,...] polyline in Angstroms, 0.1 A precision

surface_spheres.note: one sphere per up to 10 consecutive residues of Pol II, the elongation factors and the nucleic-acid scaffold; centre = mean of the window's non-H atoms, radius = RMS atom spread + 3.0 A padding. Draw as an InstancedMesh of low-poly spheres.

base_pair_register.rule: template residue i pairs with non-template residue 49 - i
base_pair_register.derivation: the single antiparallel offset that maximises the number of template-C1' to non-template-C1' contacts <= 12.0 A

transcription_bubble.bubble_derivation: template nucleotides with no non-template partner within 12.0 A, plus the template positions whose non-template partners are not modelled at all; measured from the deposited coordinates of PDB 6GMH
transcription_bubble.bubble_caveat: This is the bubble AS MODELLED in 6GMH, i.e. a measurement of this structure. It is not a value quoted from the paper, and the disordered non-template segment means the true single-stranded extent could differ by a nucleotide or two.

dna_rna_hybrid.derivation: nucleotides whose C1' lies within 12.0 A of a C1' of the other strand; a distance criterion, not a base-pair annotation, so the two counts can differ by one

duplex_axis.note: midpoints of C1'(template)-C1'(non-template) pairs, ordered by template residue, split into contiguous duplex runs; the gap between runs is the bubble

measured_b_form_geometry.rise_per_bp_note: axial rise along the PCA-fitted duplex axis of this run; the duplex is bound and bent by the enzyme, so it is not a canonical B-DNA value
measured_b_form_geometry.derivation: axis = PCA of the C1'-C1' base-pair midpoints of this run; rise = axial span / (n_bp - 1) along that axis (projecting removes the precession of the midpoints about the axis); twist = angle between successive C1'->C1' vectors projected perpendicular to that axis; diameter = P-to-P distance across a base pair (phosphate convention, so it is smaller than the van-der-Waals width)

rna_exit_channel.derivation: from the 5'-most nucleotide of the DNA:RNA hybrid to the 5'-most modelled nucleotide of the transcript; the nt count is what is RESOLVED threading the exit channel in this model, not the full nuclease-protected length

transcription_bubble.direction_note: Pol II moves along the template DNA towards +x in this frame; DNA enters as the downstream duplex at -x, is opened in the bubble, and re-anneals as the upstream duplex at +x. The nascent RNA leaves sideways through the exit channel.
